metadata.source: Evidence-Based Clinical Triage Algorithm Compilation - Educational
metadata.clinical_review_status: NOT_REVIEWED - For demonstration and preliminary navigation only. Requires formal medical director review.

rules.description: Chest pain with radiation to arm, jaw, neck, or back
rules.explanation: Reported chest pain radiating to the arm, jaw, or neck is a classic clinical indicator of possible acute coronary ischemia or aortic syndrome. Emergency intervention is mandatory.
rules.recommended_action: Call emergency medical services (911 / 112 / 999) immediately. Do not drive yourself. Rest in a comfortable seated position.
rules.clinical_notes: Immediate 12-lead ECG and cardiac biomarker evaluation needed.

rules.description: Acute focal neurological deficit (Facial droop, arm drift, or speech disturbance)
rules.explanation: Sudden onset of facial weakness, unilateral limb paresis, or aphasia/dysarthria indicates acute focal cerebral ischemia or intracranial hemorrhage.
rules.recommended_action: Activate emergency stroke protocol immediately. Note the exact time the patient was last seen normal. Do NOT administer aspirin until head CT excludes hemorrhage.
rules.clinical_notes: Time-sensitive window for intravenous thrombolysis or endovascular thrombectomy.

rules.description: Severe shortness of breath with inability to speak full sentences
rules.explanation: Inability to formulate complete phrases due to dyspnea signifies impending ventilatory compromise or critical gas exchange impairment.
rules.recommended_action: Seek immediate emergency department care. Sit upright and loosen restrictive clothing. Use prescribed rescue bronchodilators if available.
rules.clinical_notes: Risk of acute hypercapnic or hypoxic respiratory arrest.

rules.description: Inspiratory stridor or tongue/facial angioedema
rules.explanation: Stridor indicates critical narrowing of the extrathoracic upper airway, posing an imminent danger of total airway occlusion.
rules.recommended_action: Call emergency services immediately. If prescribed an epinephrine auto-injector, administer immediately into anterolateral thigh.
rules.clinical_notes: Anaphylaxis or acute epiglotittic compromise.

rules.description: Explosive sudden-onset headache reaching maximal peak within seconds
rules.explanation: Thunderclap headache is the hallmark presentation of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage or cerebral venous sinus thrombosis until proven otherwise.
rules.recommended_action: Go directly to the nearest emergency room with neuroimaging capabilities via ambulance.
rules.clinical_notes: Non-contrast cranial CT followed by lumbar puncture if CT is negative.

rules.description: Fever accompanied by severe neck stiffness and photophobia
rules.explanation: Nuchal rigidity in the presence of pyrexia is strongly suggestive of acute bacterial or viral central nervous system infection.
rules.recommended_action: Immediate emergency hospitalization for diagnostic evaluation and early empiric parenteral antimicrobials.
rules.clinical_notes: Urgent lumbar puncture and blood cultures.

rules.description: Severe abdominal pain with board-like muscular rigidity or rebound tenderness
rules.explanation: Generalized abdominal rigidity signals visceral perforation, peritonitis, or severe intra-abdominal catastrophe.
rules.recommended_action: Immediate emergency surgical evaluation. Fast (do not eat or drink anything) in anticipation of urgent intervention.
rules.clinical_notes: Immediate CT abdomen and surgical consultation.

rules.description: Frank hematemesis, coffee-ground emesis, or profuse melena
rules.explanation: Gross gastrointestinal bleeding can rapidly precipitate hypovolemic shock, particularly in patients with coagulopathies or liver disease.
rules.recommended_action: Seek emergency medical care immediately via emergency medical services.
rules.clinical_notes: Hemodynamic stabilization, type and cross-match, intravenous access.

rules.description: Sudden loss of consciousness with chest pain or palpitations
rules.explanation: Syncope preceded by cardiac symptoms raises suspicion for high-grade atrioventricular block, malignant ventricular arrhythmia, or structural outflow obstruction.
rules.recommended_action: Immediate emergency department evaluation with continuous cardiac telemetry.
rules.clinical_notes: Continuous ECG monitoring and echocardiographic assessment.

rules.description: Multiple symptoms with high severity (>=8) and rapid worsening
rules.explanation: Rapidly deteriorating multi-symptom illness at extreme severity indicates acute decompensation requiring emergent medical triage.
rules.recommended_action: Contact emergency medical services or proceed immediately to the nearest Emergency Department.
rules.clinical_notes: Rapid clinical stabilization.

rules.description: Fever in an immunocompromised host or cancer chemotherapy patient
rules.explanation: Febrile immunocompromised patients are at high risk for neutropenic bacteremia and rapid septic progression.
rules.recommended_action: Contact your treating oncologist, hematologist, or attend urgent care/emergency within 2-4 hours for complete blood count and empiric coverage.
rules.clinical_notes: Urgent absolute neutrophil count (ANC) determination.

rules.description: Unilateral calf swelling and tenderness following surgery or prolonged immobility
rules.explanation: Asymmetric lower extremity swelling is the primary clinical finding in deep vein thrombosis, carrying risk of pulmonary embolism.
rules.recommended_action: Seek same-day medical consultation or urgent care evaluation for bilateral compression ultrasound.
rules.clinical_notes: Wells DVT criteria scoring and venous duplex scan.

rules.description: High-grade fever (>39.5°C) persisting longer than 48 hours without clear focus
rules.explanation: Sustained high fevers resistant to antipyretics warrant prompt laboratory investigations to identify occult bacterial foci.
rules.recommended_action: Schedule an in-person medical evaluation within 12 to 24 hours.
rules.clinical_notes: Urinalysis, chest radiography, and inflammatory markers.

rules.description: Abdominal or pelvic pain in pregnancy or early postpartum period
rules.explanation: Pelvic pain in pregnant individuals requires exclusion of ectopic gestation, placental abruption, or pre-eclampsia with hepatic capsule distension.
rules.recommended_action: Contact your obstetrician/gynecologist or go to an obstetric triage unit today.
rules.clinical_notes: Transvaginal ultrasound and beta-hCG correlation.

rules.description: Headache, nausea, or dizziness following direct head impact within 48 hours
rules.explanation: Post-traumatic symptoms require assessment using clinical decision rules (such as Canadian CT Head Rule) to exclude delayed intracranial bleeding.
rules.recommended_action: Undergo professional medical assessment today. Avoid physical exertion and screens. Have a companion monitor for decreasing alertness.
rules.clinical_notes: Canadian CT Head Rule application.

rules.description: Moderate severity symptoms (5-7) worsening despite conservative management
rules.explanation: A steadily worsening symptom trajectory suggests an evolving pathology that has not resolved spontaneously.
rules.recommended_action: Arrange an appointment with your primary care provider or visit a walk-in urgent care center within 24 to 48 hours.
rules.clinical_notes: Comprehensive clinical review and targeted diagnostic workup.

rules.description: New headache with blurred or double vision
rules.explanation: Headaches coupled with diplopia or scotoma necessitate fundoscopic examination to rule out papilledema or temporal arteritis in older patients.
rules.recommended_action: Seek prompt medical evaluation by an eye care specialist or physician within 24 hours.
rules.clinical_notes: Fundoscopy and visual field testing.

rules.description: Mild isolated symptom (severity <= 3) of short or moderate duration
rules.explanation: Symptoms at this severity level without warning signs or progressive deterioration are generally suitable for standard outpatient evaluation or guided self-care.
rules.recommended_action: Monitor symptoms, rest, maintain adequate hydration. Schedule a routine primary care visit if symptoms persist or do not improve after 5-7 days.
rules.clinical_notes: Conservative supportive measures; follow-up if signs change.

rules.description: Symptoms actively improving with resolving severity
rules.explanation: An improving trajectory indicates that the physiological response or home measures are effectively managing the condition.
rules.recommended_action: Continue current supportive measures and rest. Contact a healthcare provider on a non-urgent basis if recovery stalls or symptoms relapse.
rules.clinical_notes: Reassure patient with clear red-flag return instructions.

rules.description: Stable chronic symptom of over 1 week duration with mild to moderate severity
rules.explanation: Long-standing stable symptoms without acute acceleration or systemic features are best addressed through a planned comprehensive primary care consultation.
rules.recommended_action: Book a routine appointment with your regular doctor or specialist for maintenance review and treatment optimization.
rules.clinical_notes: Review chronic disease management plan.

rules.description: Contradictory information (e.g. reported extreme severity but also marked as completely resolving)
rules.explanation: The information provided contains conflicting or mutually exclusive responses that prevent a coherent, safe triage determination.
rules.recommended_action: Please re-read and answer the assessment questions carefully, or contact a healthcare helpline (e.g., NHS 111 / telehealth) for interactive triage with a registered clinician.
rules.clinical_notes: Clinical reassessment required due to discordant user responses.

rules.description: Incomplete assessment with missing critical red-flag responses
rules.explanation: Essential safety questions were bypassed or omitted. A valid urgency assessment cannot safely be rendered without this data.
rules.recommended_action: Complete the required follow-up questions to receive a valid classification. If in doubt about severe symptoms, always err on the side of seeking medical care.
rules.clinical_notes: Incomplete dataset prevents automated risk stratification.
